---
name: pull-request
description: Prepare a branch and PR proposal, request separate button-based approvals for publishing and PR creation, then create the PR immediately after approval.
argument-hint: Optional spec file path; otherwise use the current changes
agent: agent
---
Prepare a pull request using the optional spec file `${input:specFile}`. If no spec file was provided, use the current changes as the source of truth.

Use the default Agent tools. Before making changes, verify terminal execution, file reading/search, and `vscode/askQuestions` are available. After identifying the hosting provider in step 2 and before committing or pushing, verify the appropriate CLI and repository access. For GitHub, run `gh --version`, `gh auth status --hostname github.com`, and `gh repo view github.com/<owner>/<repo> --json nameWithOwner,url`, deriving owner and repo from `origin`. Use GitHub CLI for all GitHub API operations, not GitHub MCP tools; CLI authentication is independent of the Copilot account and enterprise MCP connection. For Azure DevOps, verify `az repos pr create --help` succeeds and authenticated access to the target repository works. If a required tool or authentication is unavailable, stop and explain what is missing. Never request credentials in chat; ask the user to authenticate directly in their terminal or browser.

1. Run `git status` and inspect both `git diff` and `git diff --cached`. If the working tree has no changes, stop and report that there is nothing to publish. Include untracked files in the review when relevant; do not include unrelated changes.
2. Detect the hosting provider with `git remote get-url origin`. Continue only for `github.com` (GitHub) or `dev.azure.com` / `visualstudio.com` (Azure DevOps). If the remote is missing or uses another host, stop and explain why.
3. Determine the source branch and the PR's base/target branch separately. Use the repository's default branch as the base unless the user specified another target; ask if it cannot be determined. If the current branch is `main` or `master`, propose a source branch named `feature/NNN-kebab-title` based on the spec filename when a spec is supplied. If no spec is supplied, propose `feature/<short-kebab-title>` based on the changes. Ensure the name is unused locally and on `origin`, but do not create or switch branches yet. Do not change branches otherwise.
4. If a supplied or changed spec has a non-empty `work_item` URL, derive its reference from the URL: `github.com/.../issues/<id>` becomes `#<id>`; `dev.azure.com/.../_workitems/edit/<id>` becomes `AB#<id>` for GitHub and `#<id>` for Azure DevOps. If `work_item` is empty or absent, use no reference. Do not guess a reference from prose.
5. Review the changes and prepare a concise imperative commit message. Append the derived reference when present. Do not commit unrelated files or amend existing commits.
6. Look for and read any repository PR template (`pull_request_template.md` or files in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`) and use it to structure the PR body. Draft the PR title and body. The body must include a concise summary of the changes, a link to the spec when one exists, and the spec's acceptance criteria with checkboxes reflecting only criteria supported by the changes or verification evidence. Include `Closes <reference>` when a reference exists. Do not claim criteria are complete without evidence.
7. Present the proposed source branch, base branch, commit message, PR title, and complete body. Then call `vscode/askQuestions` with one single-choice question and exactly these options: `Allow commit and push` and `Block`. Set `multiSelect: false` and `allowFreeformInput: false`. Proceed only when the user selects `Allow commit and push`. If the user blocks, cancels, gives no answer, or the tool is unavailable, do not create/switch branches, commit, or push; report that publication was blocked. This approval covers branch creation/switching, the commit, and push only; it does not authorize PR creation.
8. After approval, create/switch to the proposed branch if needed, commit only the reviewed changes, and push to `origin`. If any operation fails, stop before the next irreversible step and report the failure and current branch/status.
9. After pushing, present the source branch, base branch, title, and complete body as a proposal. In the same turn, call `vscode/askQuestions` with one single-choice question and exactly these options: `Create PR` and `Block`. Set `multiSelect: false` and `allowFreeformInput: false`. Proceed only when the user selects `Create PR`. If the user blocks, cancels, gives no answer, or the tool is unavailable, stop and report that the branch was pushed but PR creation was blocked. Do not treat the commit/push approval as PR approval.
10. Immediately after the separate `Create PR` approval, run the creation command; do not stop at a draft response or ask for a third confirmation. For GitHub, run `gh pr create --repo github.com/<owner>/<repo> --head <branch> --base <base> --title <title> --body <body>` with owner and repo parsed from `origin`, the pushed source branch, agreed target branch, and approved title and complete body. Do not pass `--draft`; create a ready-for-review PR. For Azure DevOps, run `az repos pr create --source-branch <branch> --target-branch <base> --title <title> --description <body>` with explicit organization/project/repository arguments derived from `origin`; add `--work-items <id>` for an Azure DevOps work item. Pass the title and body as literal arguments, not executable shell text; preserve multiline Markdown with literal PowerShell variables or a single-quoted here-string, and never use `Invoke-Expression`. Report the returned PR URL only after successful creation. Never merge the PR.

If any required operation fails, stop before proceeding to the next irreversible step and report the failure and current branch/status. Never discard or overwrite user changes.
